cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T2 tests T1 with Vancouver; T3 narrows; T4 answers both; T6 reworks T5's warehouse analogy.
cells.limitation: T3's claim that the Atlantic current is stronger is never taken up by anyone.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 introduces storage versus transport, absent from openings; T7 builds a test on it; T9 extends it.
cells.limitation: T10 adds a general caution about memorability rather than a new distinction.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T4-T6 examine current transport against wind delivery and ocean heat storage.
cells.limitation: Nobody raises mountain-driven jet stream patterns or why Europe still beats coastal British Columbia.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T8 concedes wind and storage but adds the cold Labrador-side current; T9 folds it in.
cells.limitation: T3's Atlantic-strength point is dropped rather than reconciled with the storage view.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D ends with a causal chain and a named open question about relative weights.
cells.limitation: The open question about weights gets no observation that could narrow it within the turns.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 gives the current view its strongest form: without the warehouse the truck arrives empty.
cells.limitation: The best evidence for a residual Gulf Stream role, Europe versus Pacific coasts, is never stated.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T2 names the necessity assumption and the Vancouver case that breaks it; T3 narrows rather than restates.
cells.limitation: T7's test relies on a moved Gulf Stream, a counterfactual nobody can observe.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: Vancouver near 49 N mild, westerlies, Labrador Current, Maury crediting the Gulf Stream: all broadly accurate.
cells.limitation: T4's claim that on east coasts the heat never arrives is overstated.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T6 marks going beyond Lamb and says storage may matter more; T9 admits sizes are argued over.
cells.limitation: T3 asserts the Atlantic current carries more heat without signalling its confidence.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T3 says fair hit and narrows; T8 concedes wind and storage while keeping the cold current point.
cells.limitation: T8's concession does not say which argument, T4 or T6, persuaded the Advocate.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A flags ambiguity: single biggest cause or the full set of causes.
cells.limitation: Section E's first two branches turn on what the user wants rather than on evidence.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: The user's own comparison, Norway and Britain against Canada, anchors T1, T8 and T9.
cells.limitation: Beyond the named regions, little in the question shapes depth or framing of the turns.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E offers a quick defensible answer and a self-test, matching a wish to understand.
cells.limitation: The goal of understanding is assumed rather than linked to any use the user might have.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: No invented context; the debate stays with the stated geography and question.
cells.limitation: Nothing addresses what level of detail would serve the user's purpose beyond section A.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on headline answer, largest factor, or self-test, each with an implication.
cells.limitation: The largest-factor branch ends in check recent climate science, with no specific pointer.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D asks whether the user wanted a headline cause or a picture of the pieces.
cells.limitation: This motive question appears only in sections A and D, never within the turns.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: The popular Gulf Stream assumption is tested against Vancouver in T2 and examined in T10.
cells.limitation: Whether transport and storage are separable causes is assumed, never questioned.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T10 contrasts an easy-to-remember answer with a well-tested one.
cells.limitation: The memorable-versus-tested tension is named once in T10 and not developed.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T10 notes the Gulf Stream story spreads because it is easy to remember.
cells.limitation: The pull of the received answer is touched only in T10 and section A.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E hands the user a comparison of coastal and inland temperatures to run themselves.
cells.limitation: Section D's self-reflection prompt is offered without saying what each answer would change.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Competing explanations defined: current transport (T1), wind plus storage (T4, T6), cold current and continent (T8, T9).
cells.limitation: Mountain-steered atmospheric flow is missing as a competing explanation.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T2 states the Gulf Stream view's evidential cost: Vancouver is mild without it.
cells.limitation: The wind-plus-storage view is never shown its own cost, such as Europe outwarming British Columbia.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E proposes comparing coastal and inland winter temperatures on both oceans at one latitude.
cells.limitation: Section E does not say which result would favour currents and which wind or storage.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T9 and section D separate the agreed pattern from disputed weights.
cells.limitation: Which unknown matters most, the Atlantic heat share, is not separated from minor unknowns.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E: compare temperatures across latitude-matched coastal and inland places, a modest checkable step.
cells.limitation: Check recent climate science in section E is too vague to act on.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T5 and T6 explain heat transport with a plain truck and warehouse image.
cells.limitation: T7's phrasing about a coast with the Gulf Stream moved away is hard to parse.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T8's your westerlies points to T4; T7's that gives us a test points to T6.
cells.limitation: T9's it strengthens the pattern leaves unclear which pattern, T4's or T8's.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within range, with short T5 varying the rhythm.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Advocate, Analyst and Hunter hold distinct roles; T3 and T8 mark explicit changes of position.
cells.limitation: Analyst and Hunter share one measured register in T9 and T10.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely repeat; each adds a mechanism or a test.
cells.limitation: T10 restates T9's uncertain-weights point; section D recaps it again.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: Tension between the popular Gulf Stream story and a messier causal bundle, set up in section A.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay intellectual; nothing shows why getting the cause right would matter.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T3 says fair hit and narrows, tracing the change to T2's Vancouver case.
cells.limitation: T8's larger concession does not name the argument that caused it.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: Advocate's plain and simple and the truck arrives empty give a stubborn, likeable voice.
cells.limitation: The Analyst's voice in T6 and T9 is serviceable but flat.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T5's delivery truck and warehouse, and T6's the warehouse is the whole ocean rejoinder.
cells.limitation: T10's closing line is a general caution rather than a sharp image.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T2's could sink you sets up a challenge the Advocate answers in T3.
cells.limitation: T9 and T10 settle into calm agreement with little late movement.

strengths: T2's Vancouver counterexample tests the necessity of the Gulf Stream and forces T3 to narrow its claim.
T6's storage versus transport distinction develops the debate and feeds T7's test and T9's synthesis.
Section E gives an observable self-test comparing coastal and inland temperatures on both oceans.
weaknesses: No mind raises mountain-steered jet stream flow or why Europe stays warmer than coastal British Columbia.
The wind-plus-storage view gains ground in T6 to T9 without its own evidential cost being stated.
Section E's first two branches turn on what the user wants rather than on evidence.

symptoms.observed: Nobody raises mountain-steered atmospheric flow or the Europe versus British Columbia residual.
symptoms.evidence: cold air flowing off a huge frozen continent

symptoms.observed: Storage-plus-wind view never shown what evidence it struggles to explain.
symptoms.evidence: any coast downwind of a big ocean stays mild

symptoms.observed: Advocate's Atlantic-strength claim left unanswered and unreconciled by later turns.
symptoms.evidence: I still say the Atlantic one is stronger

symptoms.observed: Section E branches on user preference before reaching an evidential test.
symptoms.evidence: If you want a quick, defensible answer

symptoms.observed: Proposed test depends on a counterfactual nobody can observe.
symptoms.evidence: a coast with the Gulf Stream moved away should still be mild

findings.description: Attributions to Maury, Lamb and Popper are plausible and the books exist, but positions were not checkable here.
A general science question supplies little personal context, so personal relevance and self-discovery cells rest on sections A, D and E.

rubric_fit_notes: The question is a general geography explanation with no personal detail; criteria 3 and 4 were read as the user's framing and assumptions about the topic. Judgment that jet stream and mountain effects are a central omission rests on my own knowledge of the literature.
question_type_note: Read as exploratory: criterion 5 scored on competing explanations and observable tests, not a life decision.
